You can grow on TikTok for a year, hit 100k on Instagram, and go viral on X while your bank account stays exactly the same. The audience on those platforms is scrolling for entertainment, not opening their laptop to wire you $40,000. YouTube is where you scale demand after you already have it, the slowest path to a first paying client from zero.

This video breaks down attention arbitrage on LinkedIn: 1.3 billion users, only 3% posting, and a buyer base with budgets and the authority to decide same day. It covers the 5 reasons LinkedIn converts content into clients, real time-to-first-client data across every major platform, the Comment Flywheel, and the 5 step play to start from zero, plus real Distinctiva client results including a software engineer turned seven-figure SaaS founder and an agency that grew from $1.2M to $3.6M ARR.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN:
 Why TikTok grows your audience but never your revenue
 The buying intent problem that makes Instagram and X convert badly
 Why YouTube is a warehouse you open after you have demand, not before
 Attention arbitrage: why LinkedIn attention is artificially cheap right now
 The 5 reasons LinkedIn turns content into clients in 2026
 Real time to first client data across every major platform
 The Comment Flywheel and how to borrow other creators' audiences
 The 5 step play to go from zero to paying clients on LinkedIn

KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 The followers worth having are the ones with budgets, authority, and a problem to solve
 LinkedIn has 1.3 billion users and only 3% post, so the price of attention is artificially low
 Posting 3 times a week puts you in the top 3% of the entire platform
 LinkedIn buyers have a corporate card and can act on your offer the same day
 Across our clients, LinkedIn takes 90 days or less to land a first paying client
 LinkedIn in 2026 looks like TikTok in 2019, and that window is already tightening
